positive.prompt: Create the Linear project, milestone, cycle, and issues for this feature through the Linear MCP server
Reassign this Linear issue to the backend engineer and mark it blocked with a status update
Make a ticket for this request with my prompt verbatim before starting any work
File the review finding as a Linear issue and record on the ticket that the design review was skipped and why

negative.prompt: Write the PRD for this feature
Break this spec into small verifiable tasks with acceptance criteria

evals.prompt: The user says: "Add CSV export to the reports page, and skip the design review for this one." Set up the ticket in Linear.
evals.expected_output: A ticket searched for and then created under the right project before any code, carrying the user's prompt verbatim, the ticket anatomy, acceptance criteria, a scope class, the skipped design review recorded with the reason, and the identifier read back and quoted
expectations: Searches for an existing project and issue before creating
The ticket carries the user's prompt verbatim, not a paraphrase
The skipped design review is recorded on the ticket with the reason
The ticket uses the task template with outcome and verification surface
The identifier is read back and quoted, never fabricated

evals.prompt: Record an approved engineering plan in Linear. The team has existing upcoming cycles and T-shirt estimates enabled. The reviewed LLD supports a focused close-order contract issue and a schema migration issue within a usable end-to-end cycle goal. There is also a provisional future bulk-close API placeholder with no design yet.
evals.expected_output: Reads existing objects and team settings, records the design-backed focused issues with native T-shirt estimates and real cycle assignments, keeps the future placeholder blocked and unestimated, and reads back the changes. Records the cycle goal, verification, and capacity basis without altering team settings.
expectations: Reads team estimate settings and existing cycles before writing; reuses existing objects rather than duplicating them
Writes actionable issues with definite deliverables, design links, acceptance criteria, verification and native estimate fields
Uses the team's T-shirt scale and Linear effort or documented mapping rather than forcing Fibonacci labels or adding ordinal sizes
Leaves the undesigned placeholder explicitly provisional, unestimated, blocked and outside committed delivery scope
Records a usable cycle goal, end-to-end verification, and an explicit capacity basis
Reads back identifiers, native estimates and cycle assignments; reports missing tool capabilities instead of inventing success
